cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A secure login verifies a user's identity from their credentials and then gives them a session, without exposing the password or making the account easy to take over. It combines several controls, each covering a different attack.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Serve everything over HTTPS, store passwords only as salted bcrypt or Argon2 hashes, verify in constant time. On success rotate the session ID into an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie, or issue a short-lived access token plus refresh token. Rate-limit failures, offer MFA, return generic errors, and protect against CSRF.

questions.q: Why return 'Invalid credentials' instead of saying which field was wrong?
questions.a: Saying 'user not found' vs 'wrong password' reveals which emails have accounts (user enumeration), letting attackers focus guessing on real accounts.

questions.q: Why rotate the session ID on login?
questions.a: To prevent session fixation: an ID set before login must not stay valid as an authenticated session.

questions.q: Which cookie flags protect a session ID?
questions.a: HttpOnly (no JavaScript access), Secure (HTTPS only) and SameSite (CSRF protection).
